classification.reason: Track 8's architecture boundary is supported, while the exact raw Cell mode ABI, runtime ordering, and save transaction remain deferred.

scope.runtime_reason: The architecture-deciding trace is not available in the permitted corpus. Historical traces reached only bounded main-menu startup, and the host has no Xvfb path; no SPORE/ or spore.db access was performed.

hypotheses.name: merged_runtime
hypotheses.claim: cCellGame, cCellObjectData, cCellGFX, cCellUI, and cCellModeStrategy are one merged runtime object graph whose lifecycle and gameplay authority cannot be separated.
hypotheses.prediction: If true, mode Initialize/OnExit/Dispose would operate on one composite owner, and presentation release would be inseparable from simulation object release.
key_evidence: Separate global objects are assigned at 0x00e81cf0: sCellGame, sCellGFX, and sCellUI.
cCellGame::Initialize at 0x00e80ba0 resets runtime flags/pools and does not own cCellGFX/UI fields.
cCellModeStrategy::OnEnter at 0x00e552f0 calls cCellGFX::StartDisplay, while the frame orchestrator at 0x00e806b0 reaches simulation and presentation helpers in a fixed static sequence.
FUN_00e66010 releases a cCellObjectData-associated GFX object without releasing the Cell pool entry; FUN_00e780a0 later releases the old Cell object on despawn.

hypotheses.name: explicit_simulation_presentation_split
hypotheses.claim: The binary has a simulation authority based on Cell pool identity/state and a replaceable presentation association based on GFX/UI/world handles.
hypotheses.prediction: If true, a per-cell GFX detach helper should clear the association without releasing the cCellObjectData pool entry, and a separate rebuild helper should replace the GFX index on that same still-live cell. A single atomic detach→rebuild call is not required for this bounded static claim.
key_evidence: cCellObjectData is 920 bytes with mModelKey at +0xfc, mCellResource at +0x108, mGFXObjectIndex at +0x248, mScale at +0x358, and mpQuery at +0x35c.
CreateCellObject returns a cObjectPoolIndex and initializes model/resource, transform, health, scale, query, and GFX-related state separately.

FUN_00e66010 is a static per-cell GFX detach-only path: it clears +0x248 and releases the GFX record without releasing the cCellObjectData pool entry; FUN_00e6d8f0 is a separate same-cell GFX rebuild path.
FUN_00e780a0 clears sCellGame+0x411c only when it matches the object being despawned, detaches the GFX association, may create replacement/child state, and then releases the old pool object.
PlayAnimation at 0x00e6d200 returns without animation dispatch when model identity or mGFXObjectIndex is absent, but animation intent fields are stored on the Cell object when the association exists.

hypotheses.name: transient_presentation_proxies
hypotheses.claim: GFX object indices, world/layer handles, effect instances, UI rollover records, and pose/render bindings are transient presentation proxies; they are not simulation identity or durable content.
hypotheses.prediction: If true, the per-cell detach helper should leave the cCellObjectData pool entry live while removing only the GFX association; the same-cell rebuild path may then attach a new GFX record. This is a bounded static seam, not a universal runtime guarantee.
key_evidence: cCellGFX::Initialize at 0x00e5dba0 creates separate skybox, background, beach, model, effects, and foreground world/layer handles.
cCellGFX::StartDisplay at 0x00e55120 activates shadow, layer, effect-world, display, and audio-track state.
cCellGFX::InstanceEffectOnCell at 0x00e66840 creates an effect-scoped visual instance from cell.mTransform and stores it in a separate effect-instance arena.
cCellUI::ShowHealthRollover is gated by the presence of a GFX object; UI rollover records are 56-byte pooled records with a disappearance time.

FUN_00e66010 clears +0x248 and releases the GFX record without releasing the cCellObjectData; FUN_00e6d8f0 later writes a new GFX index to the same cell. FUN_00e78c00 contains mutually exclusive branches, so this is not one atomic detach→rebuild call.
cCellGFX and cCellUI have separate structures and are released through distinct teardown paths in Dispose at 0x00e81f30.

hypotheses.name: persistent_content_boundaries
hypotheses.claim: Cell content records and cCellSerializableData are durable/content or save boundaries distinct from transient runtime pool and presentation state.
hypotheses.prediction: If true, model/resource identity should be resolved from content records before presentation, and serializable state should not be treated as a Cell resource record or as a GFX handle.
key_evidence: CreateCellObject writes mModelKey at +0xfc from GetModelKeyForCellResource and retains mCellResource at +0x108 as a runtime cCellDataReference_ to Cell content; these are different classifications.
cCellGFX::PreloadResources at 0x00e666f0 traverses Cell and populate resources and preloads presentation resources.

cCellSerializableData is a 236-byte ISimulatorSerializable/RefCount object with progression, player key, counters, game time, difficulty, mission entries, and telemetry flags; it is held from sCellGame+0x5190.
FUN_00e63d10 and FUN_00e819b0 swap the serializable-data pointer in-process and then run UI/Cell initialization; neither is a recovered disk write or load transaction.

adversarial_steps.name: ownership-collapse-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A merged owner would make CellGame initialization, GFX display activation, UI loading, and object teardown one inseparable state transition.
evidence_for: The mode boundary does coordinate the objects, so a coarse caller can make them look merged.
cCellModeStrategy::Initialize at 0x00e81cf0 writes all three singleton slots and resets shared stage flags.
evidence_against: The three globals have distinct types and sizes: cCellGame 20,964 bytes, cCellGFX 90,716 bytes, cCellUI 2,372 bytes.
OnEnter calls StartDisplay but does not allocate the simulation pool; OnExit and Dispose call separate GFX/UI/Game cleanup paths.
cCellGame::Initialize has no direct cCellGFX or cCellUI field ownership in its structure.
adversarial_steps.independence: The structure layouts are direct Ghidra queries; the lifecycle claims come from separate decompiled function bodies. This is not an inference from one source narrative.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same separation is repeated across cCellGame, cCellGFX, cCellUI, and cCellModeStrategy, but the repeated observation is not counted as independent runtime proof.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Merged runtime is contradicted as an ownership model; explicit coordination with separate state owners is supported.

adversarial_steps.name: identity-and-detach-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A static per-cell detach-only path should clear cCellObjectData+0x248 and release the GFX record without releasing the cCellObjectData pool entry; a separate same-cell rebuild should write a new GFX index to +0x248.
evidence_for: CreateCellObject at 0x00e74a20 returns cObjectPoolIndex and separately stores mGFXObjectIndex.
FUN_00e66010 resolves the existing cell, clears +0x248, releases the GFX record, and does not release the cCellObjectData pool entry.
FUN_00e6d8f0 resolves the existing cell, allocates a new GFX record, writes +0x248, and replays idle animation without releasing the Cell object.
FUN_00e7c8c0 passes live cell objects to FUN_00e78c00, whose detach and rebuild branches do not release the positive-branch cell.
evidence_against: FUN_00e78c00 has mutually exclusive detach and rebuild branches; no single straight-line call was proven to detach and then rebuild the same cell.
FUN_00e780a0 always releases the input Cell object after an intermediate GFX detach, and FUN_00e7fd00 releases old cells during stage reload.
The exact runtime frequency and consumer behavior when the GFX association is absent remain unresolved.
adversarial_steps.independence: Detach-only and same-cell rebuild are separate function bodies with reciprocal field writes; despawn and reload are separate release paths. This is a static branch-limit result, not a runtime sequence.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same-cell seam is corroborated by field/pool behavior and xrefs, while the broader claim that every visual detach preserves identity is not made. Despawn and reload explicitly contradict that broader claim.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: A static per-cell GFX detach-only path retaining the same cCellObjectData pool object is supported. Same-cell rebuild is supported as a separate branch. Atomic detach→rebuild, universal identity survival, and despawn/reload identity survival are not recovered behavior.

adversarial_steps.name: transient-proxy-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: Presentation handles should be absent or replaceable without changing durable content keys or gameplay state; visual instances should have their own lifetime.
evidence_for: cCellGFX world/layer handles are stored at large cCellGFX offsets and are rebuilt by cCellGFX::Initialize.
FUN_00e66010 clears only +0x248 and releases the GFX record while leaving the cCellObjectData pool entry live; FUN_00e6d8f0 attaches a new GFX record to that same cell in a separate branch.
InstanceEffectOnCell creates a visual effect record independent of the Cell pool index and uses cell.mTransform as input.
cCellUI rollover records have their own 56-byte pool record and disappearance time; the UI function requires a live GFX association.
evidence_against: The original mGFXObjectIndex is stored in the 920-byte Cell record rather than in a wholly separate association object.
The same-cell detach and rebuild calls are separate conditional branches; no atomic detach→rebuild sequence or universal runtime identity-survival claim is established.
The exact lifetime of GFX pool slots and effect instances after logical detach is not fully recovered.
adversarial_steps.independence: The proxy conclusion combines Ghidra structures, the GFX initializer, the effect instantiation body, and the UI rollover structure; it is not based only on a field name.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Multiple presentation consumers repeat the same role distinction, but the exact retirement sequence is still unresolved.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Transient presentation proxies are supported; backend retirement and exact detach/rebuild ordering are deferred.

adversarial_steps.name: content-identity-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: Content identity should be resolved independently of GFX object allocation and should feed both simulation/resource state and presentation preload.
evidence_for: CreateCellObject resolves GetModelKeyForCellResource and stores the resulting ResourceKey at +0xfc while retaining a runtime cCellDataReference at +0x108.
cCellGFX::PreloadResources traverses Cell and populate resources and preloads models, textures, effects, and creatures.
cCellGFX::Initialize binds the preload to named worlds and layers, not to a single gameplay object.
evidence_against: The exact ResourceKey field order and package/cache precedence are not fully recovered.
Preload readiness relative to display activation is a static interface relation, not a runtime-observed completion condition.
adversarial_steps.independence: Content lookup in creation, preload traversal in GFX, and the Ghidra ResourceKey/cCellDataReference layouts are separate evidence sources.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The content/presentation split is repeated by several functions; it is convergent static evidence, not a package-load trace.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Persistent content identity is a separate owner/interface from runtime simulation and presentation proxies.

adversarial_steps.name: animation-intent-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: Animation intent should live in Cell gameplay state, while pose, skeleton, morph, render transform, and effect visuals remain downstream presentation.
evidence_for: PlayAnimation at 0x00e6d200 computes blend values and writes mCurrentAnimation, field_1B4, and field_1B8 on cCellObjectData.
PlayAnimation requires model identity and mGFXObjectIndex before dispatching to the animation backend.
Damage and death paths call PlayAnimation after mutating health or terminal state, demonstrating an event/intent boundary rather than a final pose boundary.
evidence_against: The original call that causes every gameplay animation request is not fully resolved.
The body does not prove the order of animation world update, creature update, pose evaluation, and draw submission.
adversarial_steps.independence: Animation intent writes, damage/death callers, and the separate IAnimWorld/RenderWare boundary are distinct evidence paths.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Animation writes are repeated across damage, death, hatch, and event paths; those repetitions establish fan-in, not event timing.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Clip/blend intent is gameplay-owned; rendered pose and backend animation objects are presentation-owned. Exact phase order remains deferred.

adversarial_steps.name: update-order-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: The mode update should be a typed orchestration boundary, not a single opaque gameplay loop. A visible GFX call should not be the sole authority for simulation state.
evidence_for: cCellModeStrategy::Update at 0x00e80980 delegates directly to FUN_00e806b0.
FUN_00e806b0 gates on sCellGame+0x51e0 and +0x515c, scales time, calls MovePlayerToMousePosition, calls the per-cell orchestrator, handles +0x51d8 reload, and then calls later Cell helpers.
FUN_00e7f3a0 contains the main per-cell update closure and calls gameplay iteration, animation/effect-related helpers, GFX-related helpers, and world/query helpers in a defined static body order.
evidence_against: The decompiler types and hidden-register parameters of FUN_00e806b0 are unreliable.
The runtime queue and frame timing that connect the app update message to the mode vtable callback are not observed.
adversarial_steps.independence: The wrapper, real orchestrator, and per-cell closure are separate bodies and call graph nodes; the historical event map independently confirms app-update and mode-vtable separation.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same broad mixed update is described in several reports, but no repeated report is counted as independent runtime evidence.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: An explicit simulation/presentation split is architecture-deciding, while the complete runtime update order is not fully resolved.

adversarial_steps.name: death-and-rebuild-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: Death, pool despawn, stage reload, and rebuild should be separate transitions. A death flag alone would lose pending interaction, effect/animation, avatar, and replacement state.
evidence_for: FUN_00e7a7c0 clamps health and dispatches to non-player death or player death paths.
FUN_00e7a4a0 sets field_113, selects scale-dependent death effects, plays death animations, and queues a pooled interaction record.
FUN_00e72060 sets field_113, plays death animations, stores a pending interaction at sCellGame+0x5194, and writes additional Cell/UI state.
FUN_00e780a0 performs object detach/release and conditional scale replacement.

FUN_00e806b0 observes sCellGame+0x51d8 and calls FUN_00e7fd00; FUN_00e7fd00 clears +0x411c, drains interaction and Cell state, releases GFX/association state, clears UI/effect state, reloads world/UI references, and reconstructs population/setup state.
evidence_against: Caller-specific respawn policy and the exact player-object construction subpath are unresolved.
The runtime duration between death and rebuild is unknown.
adversarial_steps.independence: Damage, non-player death, player death, queued-event dispatch, despawn, and reload are separate bodies with separate xrefs.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Multiple death/reload callers converge on 0x00e780a0 and 0x00e7fd00, which strengthens the separation but does not prove runtime ordering.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Death, despawn, pending interaction, and rebuild are distinct lifecycle transitions. The architecture must not collapse them into one alive/dead boolean.

adversarial_steps.name: save-and-reload-boundary-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A stage reload should rebuild runtime/pool/presentation state without equating that rebuild with a saved-game transaction. Durable content and serializable state should not be inferred from GFX teardown.
evidence_for: FUN_00e7fd00 clears the avatar, drains Cell/pool and UI/effect state, resets scale/advection and world references, and reconstructs runtime state.
cCellGame::Initialize obtains or reuses a cCellSerializableData pointer at +0x5190 and stores runtime state around it.
FUN_00e63d10 and FUN_00e819b0 swap or handoff serializable-data pointers in process before UI/Cell initialization.
cCellSerializableData is a 236-byte serializable state object, while Cell content records are separate direct asset records.
evidence_against: No original save/load round trip is available.
Concrete cCellSerializableData Write/Read field coverage, pointer restoration, and whether mode exit saves automatically are unresolved.
adversarial_steps.independence: Stage rebuild decompilation, serializable-object structure, and committed persistence synthesis are separate evidence sources; the static handoff is not a disk trace.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The distinction between runtime rebuild and save transaction is repeated in lifecycle, serialization, and data-model artifacts, but all share static limitations.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Separate runtime reload from persistent content/save state. The field-level save contract remains insufficient evidence.

adversarial_steps.name: teardown-and-smallest-separator-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: OnExit should be a cross-boundary mode/service transition with presentation cleanup, while Dispose is a deeper owner/service release; the smallest separator is a field/handle snapshot across create, gameplay mutation, separate per-cell GFX detach/rebuild, despawn/reload, and teardown.
evidence_for: OnExit at 0x00e7fc00 resets background/display globals, drains the transient interaction list, and calls GFX cleanup helpers and UI/space-related cleanup helpers without directly rewriting +0x411c/+0x108/+0x248.
Dispose at 0x00e81f30 conditionally performs extra cleanup, releases cCellGFX, cCellGame, and cCellUI through separate service bodies, and performs pause/unpause operations.
CreateCellObject, FUN_00e66010, FUN_00e6d8f0, and FUN_00e780a0 expose the separator fields and the distinction between a live per-cell detach/rebuild and identity-destructive despawn.
The committed lifecycle blocker explicitly requested one create -> gameplay mutate -> GFX detach/rebuild -> teardown field/handle snapshot.
evidence_against: The requested positive runtime trace is unavailable; static field/handle snapshots cannot prove callback timing, GPU retirement safety, or whether mode exit automatically persists.
adversarial_steps.independence: The direct Ghidra snapshot is independent of the historical blocker statement, and the blocker statement is independent of the current inability to reach Cell mode headlessly.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The static trace repeats field/handle relationships across create, update, despawn, rebuild, and teardown; repetition is structural convergence, not runtime confirmation.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Static per-cell field/handle separator completed: detach-only retains the Cell object, same-cell rebuild is a separate branch, and despawn/reload release old identity. Runtime separator not obtained; the modern stable-association invariant remains normative rather than universal recovered behavior.

lifecycle_trace.name: App::cCellModeStrategy::Initialize
lifecycle_trace.observed: Assigns or clears global sCellGame, sCellGFX, and sCellUI slots; resets stage flags; performs application service setup and registration. It does not by itself establish the full scene population.

lifecycle_trace.name: FUN_00e819b0
lifecycle_trace.observed: Sets the stage-initializing flag, calls cCellGFX::Initialize, creates extra shadow/layer handles, calls cCellGFX::PreloadResources, calls cCellUI::Load, then calls cCellGame::Initialize. The serializable-data pointer may be swapped before this sequence.

lifecycle_trace.name: Simulator::Cell::cCellGame::Initialize
lifecycle_trace.observed: Resets flags and timing, creates the 4096-entry pool via thunk_FUN_00bbb400(0x1000,0x1000), creates query handles, establishes world references, binds serializable state, invokes FUN_00e7fd00, and initializes additional stage state.

lifecycle_trace.name: FUN_00e7fd00
lifecycle_trace.observed: Clears the reload request and avatar index, drains queued interactions and pooled cells, releases GFX/association state, drains UI/effect state, reloads world/UI references, resets scale/advection and related flags, then invokes population/setup helpers.

lifecycle_trace.name: App::cCellModeStrategy::OnEnter
lifecycle_trace.observed: Clears mode/UI flags, calls cCellGFX::StartDisplay, enables the mode/renderer path, and performs associated service updates.

lifecycle_trace.name: Simulator::Cell::CreateCellObject
lifecycle_trace.observed: Allocates a Cell pool index and initializes position, orientation, transform, target size, opacity, model key, Cell resource reference, scale, query, health/identity, effect, and GFX association fields.

Mouse-ray movement mutates target position/orientation and moving state; damage/death mutate health and terminal state; PlayAnimation writes animation intent; the per-cell closure updates movement, AI, queries, animation/effects, and later Cell services.

lifecycle_trace.name: FUN_00e66010
lifecycle_trace.observed: Resolves the existing cCellObjectData by pool index, reads +0x248, clears +0x248, cleans the GFX record, and releases the GFX record pool entry. It does not release the cCellObjectData pool entry.

lifecycle_trace.name: FUN_00e6d8f0
lifecycle_trace.observed: Resolves the existing cCellObjectData, allocates a new GFX record, writes the new GFX index to +0x248, initializes the reciprocal cell association, and replays idle animation without releasing the Cell object.

lifecycle_trace.name: FUN_00e780a0
lifecycle_trace.observed: Clears a matching avatar index, detaches the GFX association, may use +0xfc/+0x108 for replacement/child work, and always releases the input cCellObjectData pool object. This is despawn/transition, not a presentation-only refresh.

lifecycle_trace.name: FUN_00e7fd00
lifecycle_trace.observed: Clears +0x51d8 and +0x411c, drains transient interactions, detaches +0x248 for old cells, releases old cCellObjectData entries, drains GFX/effect/UI state, and rebuilds world/scale/setup state.

lifecycle_trace.name: App::cCellModeStrategy::OnExit
lifecycle_trace.observed: Restores global background/display values, drains transient Cell interaction records, drains GFX/UI presentation state, and calls additional service cleanup. It does not directly rewrite +0x411c, +0x108, or +0x248 and is a cross-boundary mode/presentation transition.

lifecycle_trace.name: App::cCellModeStrategy::Dispose
lifecycle_trace.observed: Performs conditional extra cleanup, releases GFX world state, cCellGame, and cCellUI through separate service paths, and issues pause/unpause operations. It is distinct from OnExit and is not an in-place GFX rebuild.

separation.identity_result: The same cCellObjectData pool entry remains live at return; this is recovered static behavior for this helper only.
The existing cCellObjectData remains live and receives a new GFX index; this is a separate conditional branch, not an atomic continuation of detach.
The old cCellObjectData is released; any replacement is not the same pool record.
Old pool objects are drained and released; reload is a runtime rebuild, not a same-cell visual refresh.

authoritative_or_transient.effect: not proven to be serialized by exit/dispose

static_field_handle_snapshot.result: The static separator supports a bounded per-cell GFX detach/rebuild seam while keeping identity-destructive despawn and stage reload separate. The broader claim that every presentation detach preserves pool identity is not recovered behavior; stable CellId/independent presentation remains a modern design invariant. The snapshot does not establish runtime callback timing, GPU retirement safety, or save/load behavior.

resolution.architecture_decision: Adopt a modern design invariant of stable simulation CellId/pool identity independent of an optional replaceable presentation association. The original static evidence proves only a bounded per-cell GFX detach/rebuild seam, not a universal detach→rebuild transaction or identity-survival guarantee. Do not implement or treat this report as implementation authorization.
what_is_resolved: cCellGame and cCellObjectData expose pool-index identity and gameplay state distinct from mGFXObjectIndex.

A static per-cell GFX detach-only path at 0x00e66010 clears +0x248 without releasing the cCellObjectData; a separate same-cell rebuild at 0x00e6d8f0 writes a new GFX index. This is a bounded branch seam, not an atomic or universal identity-survival result.
Despawn at 0x00e780a0 and stage reload at 0x00e7fd00 release the old cCellObjectData pool objects; neither retains old identity.
cCellGFX and cCellUI are separate presentation/service domains coordinated by the mode boundary.
mModelKey is persistent content identity; mCellResource/cCellDataReference_ are runtime cross-boundary references.
mGFXObjectIndex and GFX world/effect/UI handles are presentation associations.
Animation intent is stateful Cell semantics; final pose/render output remains downstream presentation.
Death, despawn, pending interaction, stage rebuild, OnExit, and Dispose are distinct transitions.
what_is_not_resolved: Full runtime ordering between app update, mode vtable dispatch, gameplay, animation world update, pose evaluation, render submission, and teardown.
Whether a runtime detach→rebuild sequence is always taken when a GFX association is absent; the static seam is conditional and branch-limited.
Exact ownership/refcount behavior and GPU retirement timing for all GFX/UI handles.
Pool exhaustion sentinel, index-zero domain, and exact replacement policy across all 27 callers of 0x00e780a0.
Player-object construction and callback chain during stage rebuild.
Whole-save transaction order, cCellSerializableData Write/Read coverage, pointer restoration, and whether mode exit saves automatically.
Exact runtime event/queue timing and event-to-animation transport.

simulation: Pool-index identity is authoritative for live gameplay and is distinct from the GFX association index.
The static per-cell detach/rebuild seam supports a live Cell through separate conditional operations; universal identity survival is not claimed.
Authoritative position, target orientation, size/scale, health, query ownership, AI/target/timer state, death/terminal state, and pending gameplay interaction state.
Animation intent: current/target clip and blend/timing intent.
Explicit create, mutate, per-cell presentation detach/rebuild, despawn, death, reload, OnExit, and Dispose transitions.
presentation: Optional presentation association keyed by the simulation identity.
GFX/UI/world/effect/light/audio handles and visual instances are replaceable presentation state.
The static per-cell detach and rebuild helpers are separate branches; no atomic detach→rebuild transaction is assumed.
Pose/derived transform/render submission kept downstream of simulation intent.
persistent_content: Stable type/group/instance content identity and Cell/world/populate/effect/background content records.
Content preload/readiness independent of one Cell's visual lifetime.
runtime_resource_references: mCellResource and cCellDataReference_ are runtime cross-boundary references, not persistent content records and not GFX handles.
Keep resolved resource pointers and reference counters separate from stable content identity.
mode_lifecycle: OnEnter enables stage/display and mode state.
Update routes simulation and presentation through explicit phases.
OnExit is a cross-boundary mode/service transition that drains transient mode/presentation activity without being a Cell pool release or save transaction.
Dispose releases mode-owned service graphs and remains distinct from OnExit.
persistence_boundary: cCellSerializableData is not serialized as a Cell resource record.
Runtime pool, query, GFX, UI, and world handles are not presumed save-surviving.
Save/load requires a separate explicit codec/transaction contract.

exact_dependent_decisions.decision: Use a stable simulation EntityId/pool index separate from presentation association index as a modern design invariant; the original statically proves only a bounded per-cell detach/rebuild seam.

Allow presentation detach/rebuild to remove or replace mGFXObjectIndex and world/effect handles without changing the modern simulation identity; do not treat this as a universal original runtime guarantee because despawn and reload release old cells.
Keep animation intent in simulation-facing Cell state and make pose/render evaluation a presentation service boundary.
Keep content resolution/preload independent of a live GFX object and model the model key/content reference separately from pool state.
Retain explicit mode lifecycle phases; do not treat StartDisplay or OnExit as the entire simulation/presentation boundary.
Represent death, pending interaction, despawn, and reload/rebuild as separate transitions.
Keep Cell interaction records, App messages, UTFWin messages, and serializable state as separate event/persistence families.
Do not infer a saved-game transaction or automatic mode-exit save from serializable pointers or teardown calls.

cCellGame size 20,964, main 4096-slot pool, query/world references, and avatar index at +0x411c.
mModelKey as persistent content identity; mCellResource/cCellDataReference_ as runtime cross-boundary references.
Index-mediated avatar identity and separate mGFXObjectIndex presentation association.
The bounded per-cell GFX detach-only and separate same-cell rebuild paths, with the branch limit preserved.
Despawn and stage reload as identity-destructive release/rebuild paths.
Mode Initialize, OnEnter, Update adapter, OnExit, and Dispose as distinct lifecycle methods.
Static update/reload call shape and the sCellGame+0x51d8 reload-request boundary.
cCellGFX/cCellUI separate presentation ownership and world/UI handle classes.
cCellSerializableData as a separate serializable-state candidate, not a Cell resource record.
Animation intent writes in cCellObjectData; rendered pose/phase order remains unclaimed.
defer: Any positive original-process Cell-mode field/handle trace and runtime mode-selection order.
Whether the same-cell per-cell GFX detach/rebuild seam is always taken at runtime and whether detach and rebuild ever occur in one invocation.
Full GFX/UI/backend object refcount and GPU retirement order.

Exact cCellSerializableData write/read field coverage, pointer restoration, version/migration, and save/load round trip.
Resource manager multi-package precedence, cache eviction, and preload readiness relative to display start.
Player-cell identity, population placement, and world-object runtime execution.

blockers.blocker: No positive original Cell-mode runtime trace reaches create, gameplay mutation, GFX detach/rebuild, and teardown together.
